verses.text: After these things were done, the leaders came to me and said, "The people of Israel, including the priests and Levites, have failed to keep themselves separate from the peoples of the land and have followed their detestable practices. These are the practices of the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Amorites.

They've married women from these peoples and taken wives from among them for their sons. In this way the people set apart as holy have intermarried with the peoples of the land. The leaders and officials were the first to act unfaithfully."
When I heard this, I tore my clothes and my robe, pulled hair from my head and beard, and sat down in shock.
All who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered around me because of the unfaithfulness of the returned exiles. I sat there stunned until the evening offering.
At the evening offering I got up from where I had been sitting in humiliation, my clothes and robe still torn. I fell to my knees and spread out my hands to the LORD my God.
I prayed, "My God, I'm too ashamed to lift my face to you. Our sins have risen over our heads, and our guilt reaches the heavens.

From our ancestors' time to this very day, our guilt has been great. Because of our sins, we and our kings and priests were handed over to foreign kings, to the sword, captivity, plunder, and public shame, as we still see today.
For a brief moment the LORD our God has shown us grace. He's let some of us escape and given us a secure place in his sanctuary, bringing light to our eyes and a little relief in our bondage.

We're still servants, yet our God hasn't abandoned us in our bondage. He's shown us steadfast love before the kings of Persia, giving us new life so we could rebuild our God's house, restore its ruins, and have protection in Judah and Jerusalem.
Now, our God, what can we say after all this? We've abandoned the commands

you gave through your servants the prophets: 'The land you're going to take possession of has been defiled by the peoples who live there. Their detestable practices have filled it with uncleanness from one end to the other.

So don't give your daughters in marriage to their sons or take their daughters for your sons. Don't seek their peace or prosperity. Then you'll be strong, enjoy the good things the land produces, and pass it on to your children forever.'
After all that has happened to us because of our evil deeds and great guilt, you, our God, have punished us less than our sins deserve and let this remnant survive.
Should we break your commands again and intermarry with the peoples who do these detestable things? Wouldn't you be angry enough to destroy us, leaving no remnant and no survivors?
LORD, God of Israel, you are righteous. You've left us alive as a remnant, as we are today. Here we are before you in our guilt. Because of it, none of us can stand before you."
